item.title: A special event for the MBF
item.dc:creator: mmmnewsadmin
item.content:encoded: Wednesday 30 March was a very special night in the Euston Dining Room at Mark Masons’ Hall as W. Bro. Martin Vidler had arranged a unique event for the most recent contributors to the Mark Benevolent Fund at Vice Patron level – the initial collarette stage. Some 23 Brethren signed up to attend Martin’s fine dining evening and to receive their collarettes (and Festival breast jewels) from the Deputy President of the MBF, R.W. Bro. David Ashbolt and the PGM. Our photographs show the collarettes displayed by Martin, David and Tom and the whole group proudly sporting their collarettes and afterwards at dinner. As an additional piece of business, Martin had invited along, as his guest, Bro. Carl Fazackerley who is to be Loyalty Lodge’s next candidate for Advancement. Carl is a volunteer with St John’s Ambulance at its Wimbledon depot and the PGM surprised him with a cheque for £250 in favour of that charity, drawn on his Discretionary Fund. What else could Carl do but sign his registration form on the spot!? The Province offers its very grateful thanks to all who attended last night and to all those other London Mark Brethren who continue to donate so generously towards our MBF. Watch out for news of another collarettes presentation and dining experience later in the year. Details of the MBF Patronage Scheme can be found here. If you would like to know more or would like to start your own (regular) donations to the MBF please ask your Visiting Officer, whose details are on your Lodge Summons or available from your Lodge Secretary. item.title: Hertfordshire Mark Masons return to the Southern Hemisphere in their series of interviews
item.dc:creator: mmmnewsadmin
item.content:encoded:
VW Bro Kent Henderson PGMO, is the current Secretary of the Victoria Lodge of MMM No 47 (EC), the oldest Lodge of Mark Master Masons in Australia, and the only Mark Lodge in Australia within the Grand Lodge of Mark Master Masons of England. Wales and its Districts and Lodges Overseas.

KE - Firstly Kent, many thanks for agreeing to take part in this virtual interview. I have had the pleasure of knowing you for many years, primarily as Secretary of Victoria Mark Lodge No 47 (EC), of which I am privileged to be an Honorary member. So let me start by asking how you first became aware of Freemasonry?

KH - I joined in 1979, on the invitation of my stepfather. I was 24 years old at the time.

KE - What made you want to join?

KH - I also found out my father had been a member; he died when I was 12 years old, very sadly.

KE - What did your family and friends think of this?

KH - Obviously my Stepfather was happy, and my mother has a favourable predisposition to the Order. My stepfather was WM at the time, and my mother was involved in a myriad of social occasions as a result.

KE - Whilst I know you to be a member of most, if not all, masonic Orders and Degrees, when and why did you decide to join the Mark Degree?

KH - Yes, I am a member of all Masonic Orders, and been through the chair of almost all. I decided to join the Mark Degree a bit over a year after I was initiated!

KE - Were you Advanced into a lodge in Victoria Mark GL, or in Victoria Lodge?

KH - I joined Barwon Lodge of MMM No 77 (UGLMM of Victoria) on 14/4/80, and was installed as WM on 1/8/88.

KE - Victoria Lodge being of the EC, what made you want to be a member?

KH - I joined Victoria Mark 47 EC on 23/5/94 (and resigned from my mother Mark Lodge in the same year). The fact it was unique (in Australia), and also very weak, at that time. The challenge was to revive and save its unique warrant. That was soon achieved.

KE - As I know Victoria Lodge to be a most successful lodge, what is it that the lodge is doing that is making it so successful?

KH - Many reasons. Being a Dining Lodge helps (rare in Victoria). Having a number of fairly dynamic members, also. We draw our candidates for a small number of dining Craft Lodges, most successfully. It is very, very rare for either Victoria Mark or RAM to be without a candidate at any meeting.

KE - Is there any competitiveness with Victoria Mark GL? How would you describe relationships between the two?

KH - Extremely good. The UGLMMM of Victoria is always represented at our annual installation, usually by the incumbent Grand Master. Every year we make a substantial charity donation to the UGLMMM of Victoria “We Care” charity. The current UGLMMM of Victoria is an Honorary Member of Victoria Mark and RAM.

KE - Of all the masonic bodies of which you are a member, what office has given you the most pleasure?

KH - Hard question, but being Secretary/Scribe of Victoria Mark and RAM is right up there.

KE - I also know you to be the author of several books on Freemasonry. What inspired you to take on such time-consuming research?

KH - I was fascinated with Masonic history and organisation from the beginning. I was originally a teacher (I have a Master of Education Degree). And I enjoy writing - these things all came together.

KE - How has the Covid pandemic affected masonry here in Victoria?

KH - Well…we were largely shut down for over two years, which was difficult for many, despite all the Zoom meetings.

KE - What should we all be now doing to ensure a return to Freemasonry as we knew it before the pandemic?

KH - I think we will soon be back to normal, happily.

KE - Would you encourage others to join Freemasonry?

KH - Of course. The vast majority of Freemasons are really nice blokes; our Craft is one of the few organisations where you can share that kind of brotherhood.

KE - What has Freemasonry given you?

KH - Many friendships, but also a deep sense of worthwhile involvement.

KE - Finally Kent, may I thank you for your frank and interesting responses. It has been a pleasure to learn a little more about you personally and seek the views of a mason of considerable experience. On behalf of all within the Mark Province of Hertfordshire, I wish you every happiness in your future masonic career

Very Worshipful Brother Kent Henderson is also a published author, having written a number of books on Masonic related subjects. He has also produced and presented a number of very interesting and informative papers, including: "The English Mark and Ark Mariners the same, but very different" which can be accessed via this link

item.title: Mark Emergency Relief Fund
item.dc:creator: mmmnewsadmin
item.content:encoded:
At the meeting of Mark Grand Lodge at Freemasons' Hall on Tuesday, the Pro Grand Master, M.W.Bro. Raymond John Smith, announced that the Mark Benevolent Fund would be donating £25,000 to the Mark Inspectorate of Romania who have been working proactively in many ways to provide support and relief to their neighbours in Ukraine.

This tremendous endeavour has touched Freemasons across the Constitution and many of our Brethren are keen to add their own support by making a donation.

We have set up a Relief Chest with the M.C.F. under the name of the Mark Emergency Relief Fund and you can now make donations in a variety of ways.

We know that there is enormous support for this already. To make the administration of donations as smooth as possible, enabling funds to be transferred efficiently to where they are needed most, we ask that you note the following advice regarding donations:

For individual donations of less than £100 - please make arrangements with your Mark Lodge for these to be collected centrally and then for the Lodge to make one consolidated donation into the Fund. These consolidated donations will count toward the Lodge's M.B.F. honorifics, rather than each individuals.

Donations of £100 or more may be made by individuals directly into the fund and will count towards the Brother's M.B.F. Honorifics

In all correspondence please ensure you are donating to:

Mark Emergency Relief Fund

Relief Chest No.: MMM185622

The quickest and easiest way to donate is by scanning the QR code below or following this Link.

For a Credit Card Donation Form Click Here - remembering to use your Craft Lodge name and number, not your Mark Lodge.

For a Single Donation Form Click Here - remembering to use your Craft Lodge name and number, not your Mark Lodge.

If you would like more information about the ways in which you can donate using the digital options above, you can read the Digital Donations Guide by Clicking Here

And if you, or your Lodge, already hold a Relief Chest from which you would like to donate funds, there is a further, specific guide available by Clicking Here and a simple transfer guide available by Clicking Here

item.title: Annual meeting the Mark Province of Surrey
item.dc:creator: mmmnewsadmin
item.content:encoded:
The Annual Meeting of the Provincial Grand Lodge of Mark Master Masons of Surrey took place on Saturday, 19 March at the Croydon and District Masonic Hall.   [gallery jnewsslider="true" size="large" jnewsslider_zoom="true" ids="15340,15341,15342,15343"]  

The business of Provincial Grand Lodge commenced with the Provincial Grand Master individually welcoming the many representatives of other Provinces and Masonic Orders. These included V.W.Bro. John Bell, President of the Mark Benevolent Fund and R.W.Bro. David Ashbolt, Deputy President of the Mark Benevolent Fund, and Past Provincial Grand Master of the Mark Province of London. 16 Provinces were represented at the meeting, as well as 11 other Orders in Surrey.

The Travelling Keystone was returned to the Provincial Grand Master by Brother Keith Jacobs, who was Advanced into Weald of Surrey Mark Lodge in October 2021. He was supported by many members of the Lodge.

The Travelling Keystone was introduced in 2016 to encourage visiting and promote the exchange of good will within the Province. Its journey started in Bond of Friendship Lodge and the passport shows that it has been to many Lodges within the Province. RW.Bro. Ian said that it was to be presented later at the Festive Board to the Lodge with the highest percentage of members dining.

The Provincial Grand Master said that he had pleasure in presenting his charity award to the Lodge adjudged to have best supported the Provincial Benevolent Fund during the 2021 - 2022 financial year. He was pleased to announce that the recipient of the 2021 – 2022 embroidered Scrip Purse this year was Welcome Lodge No. 1237. W.Bro. Max Woodward was escorted to the pedestal to be presented with the embroidered Scrip Purse.

W.Bro. Ray Beadle was escorted to the pedestal to be presented with his Grand Patron Diamond Collaret. W.Bro. Steve Jones then presented the Provincial Grand Master with a cheque £5,133 towards the Festival from his regalia sales.

There were additional presentations towards our Festival from M.W.Bro. Peter Ribi; R.W.Bro. David Ashbolt; W.Bro. John French on behalf of the Allied Masonic Degrees; V.W.Bro. Arnold Long on behalf of the Order of the Scarlet Cord; W.Bro. Colin Beerling on behalf of the Order of the Secret Monitor; W.Bro. Charles Stoddart on behalf of the Royal Order of Scotland; and £3,000 from the Mark Provincial Grand Officers’ Mess. The Provincial Grand Master expressed his appreciation for the generous donations.

The Provincial Grand Master confirmed the re-appointment of W.Bro. John Vaughan Christopher French, P.G.J.D., as Deputy Provincial Grand Master of the Province. W.Bros. Richard John Knox, P.G.S.D., and William Raymond Barr, P.G.J.D., were re-appointed as Assistant Provincial Grand Masters.

A total of 80 appointments and promotions in Provincial Grand Rank were announced; as well as 15 Brethren receiving Provincial Royal Ark Mariner Grand Rank.

Following the Provincial Grand Master's address, the meeting was then called to order and closed in due form. The Provincial Grand Master, the Deputy Provincial Grand Master, and the Assistant Provincial Grand Masters, together with members of the Past Executive, honoured guests and Provincial Officers then left the Temple in procession to the echoing strains of Land of Hope and Glory, accompanied by W.Bro. Bob Soper, Provincial Grand Organist.

item.title: Kevin’s Half Marathon
item.dc:creator: mmmnewsadmin
item.content:encoded:
On Sunday, 20 March, the day after the Annual Meeting of Surrey Mark Masons, Kevin Woodward found himself in the grounds of Hampton Court in readiness for running the Palace Half Marathon. The chilly morning had not deterred runners as some 3308 massed at the start line.

Henry VIII stood outside his residence and wished us well. All too soon the call for Wave 1 runners to gather at the warmup zone was announced, shortly after which the countdown started, and we were off.

The day was beautiful with temperatures perfect for running. Kevin was wearing the colours of his running club, the Epsom Oddballs, which were the same as those of the Ukrainian flag. This felt most appropriate remembering the fantastic work the MBF was doing for the Ukrainian relief effort and that this run was in support of the MBF.

The route was very picturesque and reasonably flat. From Hampton Court they ran to Kingston Bridge, crossed the river, and ran down to Esher Station. From there, over Hampton Bridge and back to Kingston Bridge.

This time they turned away from Kingston Bridge and entered the Grounds of Hampton Court and, after several more kilometres, crossed the finish line. Two of Kevin's Grandchildren were ready at the finish line waving their banners. Final chip time for his Half Marathon was 1 Hr 36 min and 51 sec.

Article and photos by W.Bro. Kevin Woodward, P.A.G.D.C.

item.title: The 'John Hale' Mezzanine Floor
item.dc:creator: mmmnewsadmin
item.content:encoded:
We are pleased to give you an the opening of the Maryport Inshore Rescue 'John Hale' Mezzanine Floor.

This construction was generously funded by the MBF in the sum of £6,2890.00 with an additional donation of £4,000.00 by the Mark Province of Cumberland and Westmorland. The new mezzanine floor will be used both for storage and as a classroom .It will enable groups of children to be taught water safety and also volunteers of the Inshore Rescue to be taught new techniques in both maritime and swift water rescue. The Maryport Inshore Rescue is totally funded by charitable donations, it is not part of the RNLI but can be called out to assist or it may receive the first emergency call from the coastguard to a rescue in the Solway Firth if suitable.

The photograph above shows Mrs Wendy Scoon, M.W.Bro. John Hale P.Pro-G.M. and Mr Mike Messenger Operations Manager of Maryport Inshore Rescue.

item.title: Running for Ukraine
item.dc:creator: mmmnewsadmin
item.content:encoded:
I ran my 100th Parkrun today and wore blue/yellow in support of Ukraine. I had already decided to mark my parkrun milestone by also donating £1 per parkrun to a Ukrainian appeal and receipt of the email from MMH informing me of your appeal was most timely so that’s where I’ve made the donation.

A running buddy, Vanessa, did it with me also clothed in blue and yellow. This follows a sock theme, since the invasion of Ukraine I’ve been wearing a yellow and a blue sock at all meetings of M.M.H. orders. Thus far I’ve attended Mark, O.S.M. and Scarlet Cord so attired. There’s been an interesting response but so long as it raises awareness of the appeal, I’m happy.

Coincidentally I happen to have two identical pairs of these socks in my sock drawer!

With thanks to W.Bro. John Watts, P.Prov.G.J.W., Durham

item.title: Mark Portal was launched
item.content:encoded:
Mark Portal for a better communication between lodges, provinces, district lodges and grand lodges was launched in May 2022. This solution is available for all Mark Master Masons lodges all around world, free and add-on packages with annual contribution. Mark Package is absolutely free and there is no hidden cost. This package covers:
  • Google Play App for Androids
  • IOS App for Apple devices
  • Mark Master Masons public URL
  • Hononary Members page
  • Past Masters page
  • Founding Members page
  • Secretaries & Treasurers page
  • Office Bearers Page
  • The Promised Journey Page
  • Meetings Calendar
  • Online booking for dining (Apple & Google Pay)
  • Online payment for dining (Apple & Google Pay)
  • RSVP Option
Mark Master Package is available for £49 annually with above mention features;
  • Office Bearers Page > includes past 10 years
  • The Promised Journey Page > includes all departed Brethren
Hiram Package is available for £99 annually with above mention features and extensions;
  • Meeting Photo Gallery (Apple & Google Pay)
  • Annual Subs Billing (Apple & Google Pay)
Other add-on options
  • We could scan and make your lodge summons, minutes available online for the lodge members
  • We could scan and publish all lodge photos in photo gallery
  • We could interview senior members of the lodge members for video gallery of the lodge.
  • We can scan and make all your lodge archive available online on your lodge app.

item.title: A very informative MMM & RAM web site from Greece
item.content:encoded: The "Grand Lodge of Mark Master Masons of Greece and its Lodges Overseas" is a Masonic Body having under its auspices Masonic degrees exceptionally valued within international freemasonry. It is an independent Masonic Body, from the so called "beyond the Craft", but at the same time is very closely affiliated with the "National Grand Lodge of Greece" from which its members are mainly drawn. The presence of this website proves that Mark Masonry in Greece has a dynamic growth, assisting Greek Freemasons in their ascending path. Through this website one can be informed about various subjects concerning the Mark degrees and get in touch with us. We would gladly answer any questions about the Mark degrees and look forward to your feedback.

item.title: Appointment of new Rulers in GLMMM
item.content:encoded: The new Rulers in the Grand Lodge of Mark Master Masons were appointed. For the last fifteen years, M.W.Bro. Raymond Smith has given outstanding service  to our Order in various offices. In 2007, he was appointed Provincial Grand Master  for London, an office he held for four years before taking over the presidency of the  Mark Benevolent Fund until 2013. R.W.Bro. Ryan A Williams, P.G.J.W., Grand Secretary announced that the Most Worshipful Grand Master has been pleased  to make the following appointments: As Pro Grand Master – R.W.Bro. John Herbert Prizeman, Dep.G.M. As Deputy Grand Master – R.W.Bro. Francis Charles Spencer, A.G.M. As Assistant Grand Master – R.W.Bro. Prof. Denovan Keith Wilson, Prov.G.M.  for Durham.

item.title: Grand Master's Special Awards
item.content:encoded: At a specially convened Zoom meeting held on Tuesday, 15 December, the Pro Grand Master, M.W.Bro. Our hearty congratulations to all these Brethren. Past Grand Senior Deacon Anthony Francis John Ball - Warwickshire Ian Michael Crawford - Spain Thomas Hodgson - Cumberland & Westmorland Adrian Carl Hutt - Worcestershire Fraser McPherson - West Yorkshire Michael John Pescod - Northamptonshire & Huntingdonshire Clive Stephen Weston - Leicestershire & Rutland Past Assistant Grand Director of Ceremonies Frans Cornelius Alwyn Roodt - Natal Graham Peter Dearing - Buckinghamshire Past Grand Standard Bearer Patrick Donald Burridge - Hampshire & Isle of Wight David Arthur Day - The Transvaal David John Dixon - Somerset Keri John Evans - South Wales David Charles Greenway - Derbyshire Brian Peter Hamley - Bristol Paul Jones - Devonshire Stephen Jones - Derbyshire Trevor John Edward Quartermaine - Somerset

item.title: Relief for catastrophic earthquakes hit Turkiye
item.content:encoded: The Grand Lodge of Mark Master Masons of England and Wales and its Districts and Lodges Overseas donated £50,000 to the ShelterBox Foundation via MBF - Mark Benevolent Fund for two catastrophic earthquakes struck Türkiye and Syria on February 6, 2023. All the Mark Brethren and members of T. Progresif Masonluk Nizamları Derneği | Association of Progressive Orders in Freemasonry in Turkiye expressed their gratitude to British Brethren via social media accounts.

item.title: 2003 Annual Meeting of Mark in London
item.content:encoded: Provincial Grand Lodge of Mark Master Masons of London of Annual Meeting started very early with signage to put up, welcome packs to fill and rehearsals to perform it was all hands on deck! The big moment finally arrived and several hundred brethren took their seats ahead of the processions. The ProvGM’s procession into Grand Temple was accompanied by the swirl of the London Celtic Pipes and Drums. Once he was seated, it was the turn of the Worshipful Masters, Worshipful Commanders and a very long procession of newly-Advanced brethren. After which we then welcomed the arrival of the Assistant Grand Master, R.W. Bro. Prof. Denovan Keith Wilson. Photos of the meeting before we opened officially can be seen here. The business of Provincial Grand Lodge was carried out with efficiency and good humour, which saw W. Bro. Marios Stylianides invested as the newest Assistant Provincial Grand Master. After the appointment and investiture of the Provincial Grand Officers of the year, the Assistant Grand Master gave his Address. He talked about the strong relationship with the Craft and the Grand Master’s Keystone Fund. He also mentioned how much he had enjoyed the music and the processions – in particular the newly-Advanced brethren’s procession which represented the 130 or so brethren who had joined the Province this year. The AGM went on to stress that “among Mark Master Masons you will ever find friends.” The Provincial Grand Master’s Address which followed can be read here. Once the meeting ended, there were drinks in the bar before over 400 brethren sat down to dine in the Grand Connaught Rooms – the photos of which can be seen here.
